local_checks.invariant: The submit that follows a human review approval or an autonomy auto-approval must fill and submit only the values in the approved review packet (review.py:30-31 says so).
local_checks.result: Function-level harness with no browser, no network and no LLM. A packet holding one profile-sourced field (Email) passes autonomy.answers_known, and a rule with require_all_answers_known has no failures. reviewed_answers was loaded into the AnswerContext state, as Orchestrator._use_reviewed_values does. universal.run_submit then ran against a fake page and a stub analyze() that returned the Email field plus two fields that were never reviewed: a consent checkbox filled with the LLM placeholder 'yes', and Date of birth. Both were passed to execute(), click_submit was called with the LLM-chosen '#submit', and run_submit returned success=true with dry_run=false. No code compares the submit-pass fields with the packet. applier/adapters/runner.run_submit (lines 141-153) has the same pattern without an LLM.

local_checks.invariant: LLM-produced selectors, values and field types must not reach a sink beyond the page under review: a file path, URL fetch, SQL, shell or a privileged API.
local_checks.result: The LLM's selector, value, next_selector and submit_selector only reach Playwright query_selector/fill/click/select_option on the same page. File uploads use only resume_path, cfg.RESUME_PATH or ROOT_DIR/cover_letter.pdf; the LLM picks no path. No SQL, shell or fetch sink was found. LLM free-text corrections are filtered against db.profile_db.CORRECTABLE_FIELDS after the call. The profile given to analyze() holds PII only, no credentials. No finding here.

local_checks.invariant: Autonomy decisions use deterministic gates (kill switch, enabled rule, pending attempt, daily limit, dry_run), and review provenance cannot be self-asserted by the LLM.
local_checks.result: consider_auto_approval checks is_enabled, the enabled rules, pending_attempt and the daily limit, and dry_run is checked before click_submit. review._provenance labels a value 'profile' only when field_key is in the person's answered values and the value is equal, so the LLM cannot claim profile confidence by itself. Assist mode comes from a URL-only site type and blocks submit. The queue worker submits only through autonomy's Orchestrator.submit. kit.py checks the LLM's resume pick against the user's own resume ids. The weaknesses left over are recorded as hardening.

x_hardening: Autonomy rule selection uses the site type detected from page HTML markers (applier/universal.py _site_type -> applier/site_type.py _EMBEDDED_ATS). A generic careers page whose HTML contains a string such as 'smartrecruiters.com' is therefore judged under the owner's SmartRecruiters rule and counted in that site type's ledger stats. Consider binding the autonomy site type to the URL host, or to the URL-only type that apply_mode already uses.

The autonomy min_score condition uses ai_score, which an LLM computes from the attacker-written job description. Treat it as a ranking signal, not an authorization gate, and keep the deterministic conditions (require_all_answers_known, max_per_day, the daily limit) on by default for '*' rules.

applier/form_analyzer.py analyze() sends up to 2000 characters of the whole non-empty _flat profile, including identity fields such as ethnicity, disability_status and date_of_birth, to the LLM for every form page. Sending only the profile keys that match extracted field labels would reduce what a manipulated analysis can place into fields.

applier/form_filler.py _fill_one radio branch builds f"{sel}[value='{value}']" from LLM output without CSS escaping. This is not a security boundary (it stays on the same page), but escaping with _css_escape_attr would avoid misclicks.

local_checks.invariant: A download triggered by an untrusted job/ATS page must not be written to a retained or attacker-named location, must not be parsed or acted on by app code, and must not outlive the browser pass that produced it
local_checks.result: Both launches pass accept_downloads=True to chromium.launch_persistent_context (core/browser.py:59-89; runner/runner.py:440-444) and no module registers page.on('download'), expect_download or reads a Download object (repo-wide grep: 'download' occurs only for the server-to-runner resume transfer in runner/runner.py:720-737, server/routes/runner.py and applier/runner_hub.py). With Playwright 1.63 (installed driver, coreBundle.js): the persistent-context launch sets downloadsPath to a fresh mkdtemp(os.tmpdir()/playwright-artifacts-*) (coreBundle.js:39724,39760) and tells Chromium Browser.setDownloadBehavior allowAndName into that folder (coreBundle.js:38582-38587), so downloads never land in the Opera/runner profile's real Downloads folder; each file is named by Playwright's uuid, with resolveWithinRoot rejecting any escaping name (coreBundle.js:52131-52133); BrowserContext.close unlinks every download via deleteOnContextClose (coreBundle.js:51895, 15491-15497) and cancels in-flight ones (coreBundle.js:38754); the artifacts folder itself is in tempDirectories and removed when the browser process exits (coreBundle.js:39761, 9326-9331). Every app context is closed in a finally: applier/executors.py:93-97 (ServerExecutor, one context per pass inside `with sync_playwright()`), runner/runner.py:445-451 (launch contextmanager, one browser per task, entered via ExitStack at runner/runner.py:700), scraper/linkedin.py:47,60, scraper/indeed.py:51, scraper/naukri.py:56,69 (scrapers only navigate platform search/login URLs, not job URLs). A job URL that itself answers Content-Disposition: attachment makes page.goto raise 'Download is starting' (coreBundle.js:37699), which universal.py's pass turns into an ordinary failure classified by applier/failures.py and retried once by the queue worker; no code path consumes the bytes. Remaining exposure is only transient temp-disk use on the host running the browser for the duration of one pass (server pass bounded by 30 s goto timeouts and LLM/form steps; runner pass may additionally hold the browser open up to MAX_PAUSES*HUMAN_WAIT_SECONDS = 30 min while a human clears a CAPTCHA, runner/runner.py:105-107,754), with no per-download size or count cap in Playwright or the app. That requires the owner (or autonomy) to apply to the attacker's listing, is deleted at ctx.close(), and does not cross a principal boundary, so it is recorded as hardening, not a finding. A bounded loopback fixture (scratch/work/fx/dl_check.py) could not run: the sandbox's 1 GiB address-space prlimit makes the Playwright node driver abort at V8 isolate creation ('Failed to reserve virtual memory for CodeRange'), so the storage/cleanup facts above are established from the installed driver source rather than observed; nothing decisive depends on that observation.

x_hardening: core/browser.py:88 and runner/runner.py:441 enable accept_downloads=True although no code ever consumes a download; set accept_downloads=False (Chromium then denies downloads outright) or attach a page.on('download', lambda d: d.cancel()) handler in applier/executors.py ServerExecutor and runner/runner.py launch, so an untrusted ATS page cannot stream unbounded bytes into the host's temp directory for the lifetime of a pass (up to ~30 min on a runner waiting for a human). Regression case: a loopback fixture page that clicks three <a download> links; assert no file appears under tempfile.gettempdir()/playwright-artifacts-* while the pass runs.

Document in README/runner docs that Playwright redirects downloads away from the Opera/runner profile's real Downloads folder into a per-launch temp folder that is deleted on context close, so operators do not expect to find or need to clean downloaded files.

local_checks.invariant: Server-side automation that renders untrusted job/ATS pages runs in an isolated browser context with the Chromium renderer sandbox intact, no third-party extensions/sync, and downloads refused
local_checks.result: Violated by configuration: core/browser.py launch_browser (lines 59-89) launches launch_persistent_context on cfg.opera_data() (the owner's real Opera Stable profile per .env.example OPERA_USER_DATA_DIR), passes args --no-sandbox and --disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled, removes --disable-extensions, --disable-sync, --disable-background-networking, --disable-default-apps and --disable-component-extensions-with-background-pages via ignore_default_args, and sets accept_downloads=True. applier/executors.py ServerExecutor.execute -> applier/session.py _open_browser (line 783) uses this launcher for every apply/refill/submit pass; scraper/{linkedin,indeed,naukri}.py scrape() use it for scraping. No alternative isolated context exists on the server path. Whether a renderer exploit or a malicious extension actually crosses to the owner's OS account is a third-party (Opera build/extension set) fact not observable in source, so this is recorded as hardening plus a needs_validation candidate rather than a confirmed finding.

local_checks.invariant: The origin the automation fills (profile PII typed, resume uploaded via set_input_files) is bound to the job the owner queued, and nothing is handed to a page before the human review step the code promises
local_checks.result: Not enforced. applier/universal.py _click_apply_button (lines 521-551) clicks the first matching Apply selector, follows any popup via context.expect_page (line 537) or in-place navigation, and returns the new page with no comparison of its origin to job['url']; run_application (lines 153-190) then calls form_filler.execute on that page in iteration 1, before any review, typing profile values (form_filler.py lines 123-186) and attaching the resume to any file input (form_filler.py lines 95-109, set_input_files of resume_path or cfg.RESUME_PATH). The source itself states a 'human-review-before-anything-happens guarantee' (universal.py lines 42-46) but only applies it to CLICK_IS_TERMINAL platforms. Page JS on the landing origin can read typed values and the attached File before any submit. preflight.fetch_page (applier/preflight.py lines 165-188) returns (None, '') for non-http(s) or blocked URLs and _open then proceeds (lines 233-249), so preflight does not gate the scheme/origin passed to page.goto either. Selectors used for filling come from LLM output and DOM extraction (form_analyzer.py lines 28-63, 300-315) with no allowlist. Job URLs come only from scrapers (tracking/pipeline.py line 110 -> db/jobs_db.py add); no HTTP route inserts an arbitrary URL, so the attacker is the controller of a scraped listing/ATS page or of the page its Apply button leads to.

local_checks.invariant: Only the owner can cause the server browser to open pages, and the URLs opened are constrained to the scraped platforms or their listing hrefs
local_checks.result: Holds for the trigger: POST /api/pipeline/run, /api/apply/start, /answer, /submit require require_owner (server/routes/jobs.py 45-47, server/routes/apply.py 67-69, 118-120, 156-158). URLs are built from platform hrefs (linkedin.py 231-236, indeed.py 165-168, naukri.py 209-213) and are not scheme-validated before page.goto, but the href is produced by the platform DOM, not by a request parameter; a non-http scheme would need the platform to emit it. No cross-principal issue found here beyond the origin-binding gap recorded in the previous check.

local_checks.invariant: The runner's browser launch is the safer sibling: dedicated profile, sandbox intact
local_checks.result: Partially. runner/runner.py launch (lines 431-451) uses a dedicated profile dir (DEFAULT_PROFILE ~/.apex_runner/profile) and does not pass --no-sandbox, but it reuses the same _KEEP_PROFILE_ARGS (lines 113-118) so extensions, sync and background networking stay enabled, and accept_downloads=True. It drives the same universal.py passes (run_pass lines 454-485), so the origin-binding gap applies to the runner equally, although there the exposed profile is a fresh one rather than the owner's daily browser.

x_failed_attempts: h14-browser returned no result (its instruction-file read was blocked by a tool safety check); unit reassigned to a fresh hunter with no evidence carried
x_hardening: core/browser.py launch_browser: drop --no-sandbox (it is unnecessary on a desktop profile and removes the renderer sandbox for every untrusted ATS page); do not strip --disable-extensions/--disable-sync/--disable-background-networking/--disable-default-apps; set accept_downloads=False (or a downloads_path with a reject handler) since no code path consumes downloads.

core/browser.py: launch the server automation in a dedicated profile directory (e.g. data/browser_profile) as runner/runner.py already does, and copy only the scoped encrypted site cookies (load_cookies) into it instead of exposing the owner's entire Opera profile (all site sessions, passwords, extensions).

applier/universal.py _click_apply_button / run_application: after the Apply click, compare the landing page's origin with the job URL host or an allowlist of known ATS hosts (applier/site_type.py already knows them) and stop with a review-needed state on mismatch; also validate the job URL scheme is http(s) before page.goto rather than relying on preflight, which ignores validate_base_url failures.

applier/universal.py run_application: defer resume set_input_files (and ideally all typing) to the post-approval submit pass, or at least gate the file upload on review approval, so the documented human-review-before-anything-happens guarantee holds for form-based platforms as it does for CLICK_IS_TERMINAL ones.
runner/runner.py launch: same extension/sync/downloads flags as above; the dedicated profile is good but the page still runs with extensions enabled by default.

core/browser.py launch_browser: the 'tasklist' shell check (line 39) is Windows-only and silently no-ops elsewhere; on other platforms an already-running Opera on the same profile will make launch_persistent_context fail with an unclear error.

local_checks.invariant: Secrets at rest use authenticated encryption with a non-public key, and crypto-failure paths do not silently downgrade to plaintext for attacker-supplied data.
local_checks.result: Fernet (AES128-CBC + HMAC, authenticated) with key from APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY env or an auto-generated persisted data/.master.key chmod 600 (core/crypto.py:50-71). encrypt() prefixes 'enc:'. decrypt() returns '' on InvalidToken (fails closed, no plaintext leak) and logs the cause once without the key. decrypt_bytes() returns the input unchanged only on InvalidToken — a deliberate migration path for pre-existing plaintext cookie files; callers that matter re-validate the result (resumes_db enforces a %PDF- signature; cookie loader json.loads which fails on ciphertext). No static IV / ECB / unauthenticated mode; no hardcoded key.

local_checks.invariant: Every secret setting is classified as secret, stored encrypted, masked on read, and cannot be read back verbatim.
local_checks.result: is_secret_key (db/settings_db.py:46) flags any key containing 'api_key' or ending _token/_password, covering all provider keys, custom-provider keys, notify_smtp_password and notify_telegram_bot_token. write() encrypts secret values at rest (line 612); _maybe_decrypt decrypts only internally. GET /api/settings masks secrets to a dotted prefix plus the last 4 chars (server/routes/settings.py:35); GET /api/settings/raw/{key} hard-refuses secret keys with 403 (line 58); GET /api/settings/providers and all_providers return no key material (test_custom_provider_lifecycle asserts the raw key is absent). save_settings skips blank/masked secrets so a re-submitted mask cannot clobber the stored key. No full secret reaches a client-visible response.

local_checks.invariant: Runner bearer tokens use strong randomness and are stored/compared as non-reversible hashes with no timing side-channel on the secret.
local_checks.result: new_token() = 'apxr_' + secrets.token_urlsafe(32) (256 bits CSPRNG; db/runner_db.py:109). Only SHA-256(token) is stored (UNIQUE), shown once on creation; authenticate() looks up by digest on an indexed column and never returns or logs the token. parse_bearer requires exactly 'Bearer <token>', rejects other schemes; length-capped at 200 before hashing. Revocation and account-active are re-checked on every authenticate. No weak randomness, no reversible storage.

local_checks.invariant: Job-site cookies and resume PDFs/text are encrypted at rest, and reads refuse unauthenticated-plaintext substitution.
local_checks.result: save_cookies encrypts the cookie JSON with encrypt_bytes (core/browser.py:124); load_cookies decrypts, tolerating legacy plaintext only via the Fernet-token check. Resumes: PDF bytes and extracted text both encrypted (db/resumes_db.py:200-203); random on-disk filename; read() refuses a stored file that still starts with %PDF- (never encrypted) and refuses output that does not decrypt to a %PDF- signature, so a dropped-in plaintext file is rejected rather than used. Plaintext exists only in a 0700 tmpdir/0600 file inside a with-block with guaranteed cleanup and stale sweep.

local_checks.invariant: Notification secrets are masked in responses and never written to logs, error messages, or outbound URLs that surface to clients.
local_checks.result: public_config replaces notify_smtp_password and notify_telegram_bot_token with a mask (core/notifier.py:124-131); GET/PUT /api/notifications/settings are require_owner and return only public_config. Delivery failures are logged by exception TYPE only (deliver line 288, test_channel line 312), and DeliveryError/NotifyError are documented and coded to carry no secret or server reply; the Telegram bot token lives in the request URL but that URL is never logged or returned. SMTP host is re-validated at send time (validate_smtp_host).

x_hardening: GET /api/settings (server/routes/settings.py:35) returns a dotted prefix plus the last 4 characters of each DECRYPTED secret (API keys, notify_smtp_password, notify_telegram_bot_token). Last-4 masking is industry-standard for high-entropy keys but is still cleartext secret material in a client-visible response; for user-chosen secrets like an SMTP password consider masking with no trailing cleartext.

POST /api/auth/logout (server/routes/auth.py:82) only clears the cookie and does not bump session_version, so a signed session token obtained out-of-band remains valid for its full 14-day max_age after the user logs out; change-password and logout-everywhere do revoke server-side. HttpOnly+Secure limit token capture, but bumping session_version on logout would give parity and true revocation.

WebSocket /ws/{job_id} (server/websocket.py:57) authenticates the session and enforces job ownership but performs no Origin allowlist check; cross-origin hijack is currently prevented only by the SameSite=Lax session cookie not being attached to cross-site WS handshakes, and the handler is read-only. An explicit Origin/Host check would add defense in depth independent of browser SameSite behavior.

The application has no CSRF token and no Origin/Referer validation on any route (server/app.py); CSRF protection relies solely on the explicit SameSite=Lax session cookie (core/auth.py:145). This is effective for the non-GET JSON/multipart mutations actually used, but it is a single layer — an anti-CSRF token or Origin check on state-changing routes would harden against future SameSite regressions or a route added with a Lax-permitted method.

The session throttle (core/throttle.py) is in-memory and per-process and the login IP is request.client.host; behind a reverse proxy without uvicorn --proxy-headers/--forwarded-allow-ips every client shares one bucket. This is documented in the module and is a deployment-config concern, not a source defect.

local_checks.invariant: validate_base_url rejects every spelling of a cloud-metadata or link-local host that the outbound HTTP client will connect to

local_checks.invariant: A URL that passed validate_base_url cannot be redirected by the remote end to a blocked address
local_checks.result: Not enforced: a loopback 302 to 169.254.169.254 was followed by preflight.fetch_page (urllib, preflight.py:172-181) and by the OpenAI SDK (follow_redirects default). Blind impact only (response feeds the closed-job check or an owner-visible error; httpx strips Authorization cross-origin; GCP/Azure metadata need headers not sent). Recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: Untrusted content cannot pick the destination of a server-side preflight fetch or Playwright goto
local_checks.result: Job URLs enter only via the owner's scrape pipeline (only INSERT INTO jobs at db/jobs_db.py:415 from tracking/pipeline.py), built from the board's own card href with the board base URL; set_hunt cannot change url; preflight/apply start only from require_owner routes (apply.py:69,120,158) or the owner's queue. A job poster has no source-visible control of job['url'] host.

local_checks.invariant: SMTP and Telegram sinks cannot be steered to metadata or arbitrary hosts
local_checks.result: SMTP host validated at save (notifier.py:192) and before connect (notifier.py:242); Telegram URL has fixed host api.telegram.org with regex-checked token/chat id (notifier.py:265-268); owner-only configuration.

x_hardening: core/urlcheck.py validate_base_url (104-107) accepts hosts written with IDNA label separators (U+3002, U+FF0E, U+FF61), e.g. http://169。254。169。254/; httpx/OpenAI connect to 169.254.169.254 (owner-only input). Fix: reject non-ASCII hosts or IDNA/UTS46-encode before the IP/blocklist checks.

Redirects are followed without revalidation: applier/preflight.py fetch_page (urllib) and the OpenAI clients in core/llm.py (follow_redirects=True). Fix: a redirect handler that revalidates, or httpx.Client(follow_redirects=False).
applier/universal.py page.goto(job['url']) (111, 247, 342) has no scheme/host check; add the same http(s)/no-metadata check as preflight.
validate_base_url does not check DNS resolution (documented at core/urlcheck.py:16-19); a connect-time check in a custom transport would close it and the redirect gap.

local_checks.invariant: No caller-supplied value or key becomes SQL text. Dynamic identifiers (SET column lists, INSERT columns, WHERE fragments, IN placeholders) must come only from fixed allow-lists or placeholder counts.
local_checks.result: Every f-string or concatenated SQL in db/ uses only fixed allow-lists or placeholder counts: set_hunt (hunt.HUNT_FIELDS via clean_hunt), offers create/update (clean_offer allow-list), autonomy update_rule (UPDATABLE_RULE_FIELDS), the follow_ups and prep _change/_finish sets (constant literals), IN lists ('?'*n), _and/_where (constant column), list_applications stages (validated against lifecycle.STAGES), answer_bank scope/source (validated) and LIKE values (bound, with ESCAPE), and ALTER TABLE (constant column list). The sandboxed harness against a temp jobs.db with two dummy users confirmed this. Injected keys were rejected by set_hunt, offer create/update and autonomy update_rule. Stage, scope and source payloads raised ValueError. q, source and title payloads (including '%') were bound literally and returned no rows. A cross-user set_hunt raised LookupError. The DB rows were unchanged: user 2's job and the offer user_id were intact.

local_checks.invariant: Key-value stores whose keys come from requests (settings keys, profile field keys, custom-provider slugs) must bind those keys as parameters, never interpolate them.
local_checks.result: Settings, profile, users, review, resumes and outcomes queries all use ? placeholders for keys and values. The custom-provider f-strings in settings_db.py:421-581 build key VALUES that are then bound, not SQL text. Routes in server/ issue no SQL directly, and no SQL runs outside db/ (grep over server, core, applier, intelligence, tracking).

local_checks.invariant: No shell, header, message-format or template injection from stored data into secondary systems.
local_checks.result: The SMTP path uses EmailMessage with the default policy: header values are a constant-format Subject plus owner-set From/To, and the policy rejects CR/LF in headers. Telegram sends JSON {chat_id, text} with no parse_mode, so the text is not interpreted as markup. Subject templates are constants formatted only with integers (notifier.py:324). The only shell=True call is the constant 'tasklist' (browser.py:39). taskkill/Popen use argument lists with a PID or internal argv. Playwright launch args are constants; cookie files are encrypted JSON passed to add_cookies.

x_hardening: frontend/src/components/applications/Workspace.jsx:33 and SidePanel.jsx:96/116: the ?job= query value goes unencoded into fetch paths, which is a client-side path traversal primitive (../../../api/settings?x= resolves to /api/settings). The only reachable unsafe request today is a victim-clicked Notes POST with the fixed body {note}, which has no security effect. Wrap jobId in encodeURIComponent, or validate ^[0-9a-f]{16}$ before setOpenId, so a future GET+POST endpoint cannot be reached this way.

server/app.py sets no X-Frame-Options / CSP frame-ancestors. Clickjacking is currently blocked for cross-site framers by the SameSite=Lax session cookie (core/auth.py:145), but a same-site origin (e.g. another port on the same host) could frame the Approve/Submit UI. Add 'Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors none' (and X-Frame-Options: DENY) in a response middleware.
templates/setup.html:243 builds row.innerHTML from interpolated values with no escaping. It is not served today; delete the file so it cannot be re-mounted.
safeHref (frontend/src/lib/live.js:65) correctly limits job links to http(s), but any http(s) destination is allowed. That is acceptable because every anchor uses rel=noopener noreferrer.

Do the count check and the append in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction.

core/resume_parser._extract_text has no page or character cap of its own, while db/resumes_db.extract_text has one. Apply TEXT_PAGES/TEXT_CHARS-style limits there too, and stop iterating once enough text is collected.

local_checks.invariant: A runner bearer token is checked (prefix, length, SHA-256 lookup, not revoked, user active) and binds the request to exactly that token's user_id and token_id
local_checks.result: parse_bearer accepts only 'Bearer <tok>'. authenticate looks up hash_token(raw) by exact match, refuses a revoked token or an inactive user (users_db.get_by_id filters is_active=1), and returns the stored user_id and token_id. Every RunnerHub, RunnerTaskStore and RunnerTokenStore query is scoped by that user_id. require_runner reads only the Authorization header, so a session cookie does not authenticate there and a bearer token does not authenticate elsewhere. The one gap is that this check runs once per request (see the claim check).

local_checks.invariant: Only the owner can mint, list or revoke runner tokens. Revocation is scoped to the caller's own tokens. The cap of 10 live tokens holds.
local_checks.result: All three token routes depend on require_owner. RunnerTokenStore.revoke and list filter by user_id. create counts live tokens before inserting. A non-owner cannot obtain a token, so every token acts as user 1.

local_checks.invariant: The session-gate bypass covers only the 5 runner endpoints, and no other handler can match those paths
local_checks.result: RUNNER_PATH is fullmatched against /api/runner/(claim|<32 hex>/(events|screenshot|result|resume)). No other router declares an /api/{param} or :path route that could match these paths. Token management lives under /api/settings, behind the session gate.

local_checks.invariant: Per-task binding: events, screenshot, result and resume act only on a task currently claimed by the same token. A duplicate or stale result is refused.
local_checks.result: _claimed uses get_claimed (status=claimed AND claimed_by=token_id AND user_id). complete() is a conditional UPDATE, so a repeated or late result after a requeue gets a 409. sweep() never re-queues a claimed submit (lost_submit leads to needs_you). A screenshot path is generated by the server, and clean_result uses only the task's own stored screenshots.

local_checks.invariant: The claim long poll is bounded to 25 s, and a revoked token stops receiving work at once (the docstring says 'revoked, which stops it at once')
local_checks.result: Failed. The body {"wait":"nan"} passes float(), and the min/max clamp keeps NaN, so the deadline and remaining time are both NaN. 'remaining <= 0' is never true and Condition.wait(nan) returns immediately. The poll spun for 28 s with 84958 sweep() calls, each opening a BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, while holding the token's polling slot (a second poll got 429). After the owner revoked the token, fresh requests got 401, but the open poll stayed alive. When an application was queued later, it claimed the task under the revoked token id and returned HTTP 200 with the full payload (profile, answers, kit, resume metadata).

x_hardening: Changing the password or bumping session_version (db/users_db.py change_password) revokes browser sessions but not runner tokens. Consider revoking or flagging runner tokens on password change.
RunnerTokenStore.revoke does not release tasks claimed by the revoked token. They stay claimed until the 120 s lease lapses, and a submit task then becomes lost_submit (needs_you).

clean_result always sets the dry_run key, so Orchestrator.finish_pass lets the runner's reported dry_run=false override a submit task created with dry_run=true. The job is then recorded as submitted and counted against the daily limit. The server should not let a result turn a dry-run task into a real submission.

No owner action (skip or transition) cancels a claimed runner task, and finish_pass does not re-check the job stage before running the finishers. A runner's heartbeats keep getting 200 after the owner skips the application, so the runner never gets the 404/409 'drop it' signal it supports, and its result is still processed.

Check-then-act on MAX_SCREENSHOTS_PER_TASK and MAX_EVENTS_PER_TASK, and add_screenshot's read-modify-write of the JSON list without BEGIN IMMEDIATE, allow concurrent uploads to exceed the cap and lose list entries, leaving untracked files. Belongs to the peer unit for runner screenshot resource handling.

The runner client does not check the format of server-supplied job_id and task_id (job_id becomes part of a local screenshot path via applier/screenshotter.py), and it does not re-check that application.url is http(s). Validating hex ids and the scheme client-side would add defence in depth.
The runner only warns when --server is plain http on a non-loopback host, so the bearer token travels unencrypted.
